newsitem.title: GERMANY: German employers urge pro-job investment policy.
newsitem.headline: German employers urge pro-job investment policy.

text.p: German employer and industry groups on Thursday urged the Bonn government to adopt pro-investment policies after unemployment surged to a new post-war record in January.
"The latest unemployment figures dramatically underline the need decisively and quickly to improve conditions for investment," the Federal Employers Association (BVA) said.

The BVA urged Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government to implement planned tax reforms and reduce social security costs quickly. They added that this year's increase in pension charges showed how great was the pressure to act.
The Federal Labour Office said the unadjusted unemployment figure in January rose by half a million to 4.66 million from December.
Seasonally adjusted, the figure rose by 160,000 to 4.32 million -- three times faster than expected by independent economists polled by Reuters.

Separately, Hans-Peter Stihl, head of the Chambers of Industry and Commerce (DIHT), warned that over a quarter of industrial companies would move production abroad this year, fleeing high German costs.
"Shifting production abroad does not necessarily mean job losses in Germany. But it is a clear signal: Production in Germany is too expensive," Stihl told the Koelnische Rundschau newspaper.
